# Common Parcel

> HOA management software for self-managed homeowners associations. It reads an
> association's own governing documents and then runs the dues, notices,
> violations, elections and vendor contracts on the schedule those documents and
> the relevant state statute already set. From $10 a month. Built in Detroit,
> Michigan; available anywhere in the United States.

Common Parcel is built for volunteer boards that run the association themselves,
without a property management company, a bookkeeper, or a designated software
person. It serves homeowners associations, condominium associations, planned
communities, and civic or neighbourhood associations of five to a thousand-plus
doors.

Contact: jesse@commonparcel.com — the founder answers.
Site: https://commonparcel.com/

## What it does

A board uploads its declaration, bylaws, rules and owner roster. Common Parcel
reads those documents and extracts the numbers that govern everything else — the
assessment amount, the due date, the grace period, the late fee, the meeting and
voting rules — and shows each one with the page and line it came from. Setup
usually takes about thirty minutes.

From then on it runs the association's recurring work automatically:

- Invoices dues and collects them by autopay, ACH or card
- Posts receipts to owner ledgers and reconciles the bank
- Applies late fees and issues delinquency notices and payment reminders
- Logs violations with photo and citation, and tracks cure windows
- Carries architectural review requests on statutory response clocks
- Tracks vendor contracts and bid notices
- Supports elections with electronic ballots and proxies, and tracks quorum
- Sends meeting notices and records minutes
- Writes supported administrative, dues, and governance actions to a numbered audit log

## What the board still does

Anything with legal or financial weight stops for a person. Consequential actions
such as notices, fines, and liens require two distinct current officers where the
workflow enforces the gate; there is no batch approval and no way for the
software to sign on the board's behalf. A typical month leaves the board two
decisions and about twenty-two minutes of work.

## Custody of funds

Direct settlement with zero software custody. Owners pay through an
association-connected Stripe account directly to the association's own
depository bank account. Common Parcel does not hold association funds,
maintain platform balances, or sit in custody of money.

## Citations

Citations on verified rules. When Common Parcel indexes a statute or attaches
declaration rules, it cites the exact section. If a citation cannot be verified
in the association's recorded documents or state code, Common Parcel marks it
unverified rather than guessing.

## Pricing

Graduated per lot, per month, like a tax bracket: $2.50 each for the first 10
lots, $1.10 for lots 11 to 70, $0.40 for lots 71 to 500, and $0.50 above 500,
with a $10 monthly minimum.

- A four-lot association pays $10 a month
- A 100-lot association pays about $110 a month
- A 1,000-lot association pays about $513 a month

Everything is included — collections, violations, elections, vendor management,
documents, and timestamped activity logs with archive manifest reports — with
no feature tiers and no per-notice charge. Owners pay no fee to pay their dues.
Civic and neighbourhood associations pay a reduced rate. Billing is month to
month with no contract, no setup fee, and a full export of ledgers, documents,
minutes, and audit records with manifest reports available at any time.

## Comparison

Common Parcel extracts parameters from the association's recorded governing
documents, assists volunteer boards through recurring workflows, and maintains
an attributed record for every recorded action.

## Migration

Common Parcel provides transition checklists and loads the ledgers, documents,
and rosters the association receives during onboarding.

## Status

Common Parcel is onboarding founding associations now.
